html:
Sarekat Islam was a mass organisation founded in 1912 in Surakarta, central Java, at first by batik traders resisting Chinese competition. Under H.O.S. Tjokroaminoto it became the first mass political movement in the Dutch East Indies.

By 1919 it claimed millions of members, uniting people under Islam against colonial rule. The young Sukarno lived in Tjokroaminoto's house as a student.

A communist wing split from it in the early 1920s and formed the Communist Party of Indonesia, while others joined new nationalist parties. It showed that Indonesians could organise across the islands, leading to the Youth Pledge of 1928. See Muhammadiyah.
